name: Fluticasone/salmeterol
mechanism: Dual action: Fluticasone (ICS) - suppresses airway inflammation, reduces mucus, decreases bronchial hyperresponsiveness. Salmeterol (LABA) - long-acting bronchodilation via beta-2 receptor agonism, improves lung function for 12 hours
dosing: Asthma adults: 50/100, 50/250, or 50/500 mcg BD via Accuhaler (DPI) or MDI. COPD: 50/500 mcg BD. Step up/down based on control. Rinse mouth after use. Not for acute relief - patients need separate SABA. Device-specific technique crucial
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for acute asthma/COPD exacerbation or status asthmaticus. Caution: active/quiescent TB, severe cardiovascular disease, QT prolongation, hyperthyroidism, DM, hypokalaemia
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, ketoconazole) ↑ fluticasone exposure - avoid strong inhibitors or use with caution. Beta-blockers antagonize salmeterol. MAOIs, TCAs ↑ cardiovascular effects. Other LABAs - avoid duplication
monitoring: Peak flow/spirometry, symptom control (day/night), exacerbation frequency, inhaler technique, SABA use (<3x/week if controlled). Growth in children (annual height). Signs of oral candidiasis. Adrenal suppression with high-dose ICS. Cardiovascular effects (palpitations, arrhythmias)
pregnancy: Benefits usually outweigh risks. Poorly controlled asthma poses greater risk to mother/fetus than ICS/LABA. Continue if asthma well controlled. Monitor closely. Prefer beclometasone as most pregnancy data for ICS, but fluticasone acceptable. Salmeterol less studied than salbutamol but likely safe
sideEffects: Common: oral candidiasis (rinse after use), hoarse voice, headache, palpitations, tremor, muscle cramps. ICS effects: adrenal suppression (high dose, prolonged), growth retardation (children), osteoporosis (very high dose). LABA effects: tachycardia, arrhythmias, hypokalaemia (high dose), paradoxical bronchospasm (rare)
pharmacokinetics: Delivered via inhalation. Fluticasone: minimal systemic absorption (<1%), extensive first-pass metabolism. Salmeterol: low systemic bioavailability (5-10%), duration 12h. Both hepatically metabolized (CYP3A4)
clinicalPearls: Brand names: Seretide (various strengths), AirFluSal (generic). LABA must always be with ICS (never alone in asthma - increases mortality risk). Rinse and spit after use to reduce candidiasis/dysphonia. Not a reliever - patients MUST have SABA for acute symptoms. Available as Accuhaler (DPI - breath-actuated, needs good inspiratory effort) or MDI (pressurized, may need spacer). Check technique at every visit. Step down therapy once stable 3 months - may reduce ICS dose or frequency. If not controlled on 50/500 BD, add LAMA/LTRA or refer. COPD: reduces exacerbations but doesn't affect mortality - balance against pneumonia risk. MART regimen not applicable (MART uses formoterol, not salmeterol)
indication: Asthma (regular preventer therapy, step 3+ - inadequate control on ICS alone), COPD (FEV1 <50% with exacerbations despite LABA/LAMA)
